judgments.reasoning_cat1: The holiday span is defined precisely, though the second sentence's 'time and one-half the holiday rate' compounds an already doubled rate in a way that invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7-C sets holiday pay at not less than two days' pay plus time and one-half of the holiday rate, so the two premium formulas must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'thereafter price and one-half of the holiday rate' is a plain typographical corruption of 'time and one-half' that goes to the pay formula, and the base for 'the holiday rate' is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 'Section 18-B.2' for sick leave, which does not exist — the intended reference is 13-B.2 — and 7-B supplies a competing overtime formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise eligibility test based on days worked in specified payroll weeks.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 20-D expressly builds on 7-D for Group 1 men taking vacation over a holiday, which is workable but adds a discounting rule not found here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short double-time rule with a clear trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7-C already requires not less than two days' pay for holiday work, so whether 7-E adds to or merely restates that entitlement is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An anti-offset rule stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-B.2 and 13-H treat compensation absences for other purposes, and 22-F/22-G contain analogous anti-offset rules for pensions and life insurance; all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Provided these activities do not interfere with the performance of their duties' is qualified by a carve-out in the same sentence, leaving the residual scope of 'interference' vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8-C adds an overtime non-discrimination rule and 8-B bars chapel meetings in working hours, both consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete inspection rights with definite time limits; the three-week look-back proviso is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3-A.3 and 4-G posting duties and with the Newspoint/Times side letters on posting job descriptions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Insofar as the distribution of overtime' is grammatically incomplete but the meaning is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-M allows challenges to unfair overtime distribution generally; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The unit's entitlement begins only 'after such parts or sections reach the platform', a boundary line that is workable but consequential.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9-B qualifies the bulk-delivery obligation with cost and jurisdictional escape clauses, so who performs the bulk leg is governed by a much weaker duty than this section implies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall endeavor' plus 'providing doing so does not involve the Publisher in increased cost or a jurisdictional conflict' makes the obligation nearly unenforceable and turns on undefined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It softens 9-A's apparently mandatory bulk-delivery rule and echoes 2-E.2(g)'s jurisdictional escape; the two sections read together are hard to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Upon such terms as may be agreed upon between such boys and the Publishers' leaves the terms wholly open and outside the contract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-A.1's exclusive recognition and 2-M's ban on engaging helpers sit awkwardly with a class of non-union workers aiding routemen.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition tied to hours specified later; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'In aid of and under the direction of a route man' is in direct tension with 2-M's rule that no employee shall engage any person to aid him.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An absolute one-line prohibition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10-D limiting half-day boys to afternoon papers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise hours with a Saturday exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 10-B and 10-C; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line prohibition; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10-B's 'in aid of' role and 2-A.1 plant jurisdiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An administrative listing requirement; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 4-G and 2-A.2's vending-machine lists; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Now employed' and 'at this time' fix the cap to an unstated historical baseline, which is the classic frozen-practice ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10-J allows an increase on a new route with Board consent, an express exception; 10-H requires reduction — the three fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite consequence on route discontinuance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10-G's cap and 10-I's merger provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Leaves disposition to negotiation with a Board fallback; open-ended but procedurally complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 10-G/10-H and Section 16 referral practice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Good cause shown' is a soft standard, but consent of the Board is a hard gate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An express exception to 10-G; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any assistance in the matter of deliveries or distribution' is broad and undefined, and 'directly or indirectly' widens it further.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 11-B routes disputes to the Board, and 16-N permits a strike against a non-complying party; consistent scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short referral clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-A and 11-A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent permitted by law' and 'or is willing to enter into written collective agreement' leave the prohibition's practical bite uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12-B's independent-contractor rule and 3-E's methods-and-extent freeze cover related ground; a side letter says the agreement prohibits subcontracting of unit deliveries 'except as it may exist pursuant to the contract'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate referral sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule turns on delivering 'only one newspaper, though he may be delivering magazines as well', and closes with the unbounded caveat 'present practices excepted, however'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deeming such a person 'an employee of the Publisher ... subject to all the terms and conditions hereof' collides with the wage, seniority and contribution machinery in Sections 4, 13-A and 13-I.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practices' and 'good cause shown' are vague, and the OCR corruption of the middle of the sentence obscures the object.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates 3-G almost word for word, which raises a redundancy/whole-instrument question but not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'financial benefits' is a closed list ('shall include only'), yet the caps in item 3 and the '380 days' figure are garbled, and the Publisher's secondary liability depends on the wholesaler's separate contract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 18's suspension and merger pay for the Publishers' own situation holders and 12-D.2/12-D.3 successor rules must be read together with this; the interaction is intricate but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable and expeditious arrangements' and 'fully and promptly' are soft, but the clause is only a savings provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12-D.1's 'unless paid by a successor' carve-out and 12-D.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall endeavor to have said successor make the payments' is a best-efforts duty with no enforceable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements 12-D.1's mandatory Publisher liability for a narrower trigger; the difference in strength is deliberate rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A rate table with several OCR-corrupted figures, so the actual numbers cannot be read reliably from this text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A.4's cost-of-living additions, 13-E's over-scale rates and 13-C's floor for non-covered work all key off these scales; consistent in design.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same table format with corrupted figures, plus a $6.00 fringe allocation whose destination ('Pension or Welfare Fund, or both') is left to later election.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H.1's escalating $6/$7/$8 per-shift additional welfare contribution covers similar ground and could be confused with this allocation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A third rate table with garbled figures; the 'Long Night' weekly figure of $449.97 versus a day weekly of $449.72 is internally odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent in structure with 13-A.1 and 13-A.2 and with the 5-B/5-D shift definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula is spelled out with dates, an index and a 6% threshold; 'premiums and fringes such as ... etc.' is an open-ended list but the mechanics are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly feeds pension and welfare contributions under 13-H.1 and 13-I.1, which are percentage-based, so its interaction with those clauses is deliberate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prohibit, nullify or reduce any scheduled wage increase' is a clear trigger for a unilateral termination right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 19 fixes a firm term to March 30, 1984 and 17-B provides that illegal provisions merely become inoperative — this termination right is a marked departure from both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'More Than / Fewer Than' bands are non-contiguous as printed (e.g., 6–20 then 19–32, and 223–225 then 224–), leaving gaps and overlaps in the schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-B.4 caps vacation at twenty days and 13-B.2 defines what counts as days worked; the table's top band ties out at 20 days.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but mostly mechanical; 'the spirit and purpose of this provision is to disallow the duplication of vacation credits' invites purposive argument, and 'arranged at the convenience of the employer, but on the basis of seniority' pulls in two directions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 20-D gives the Foreman discretion to schedule vacations 'using seniority', and 13-B.3 preserves present splitting practices — three overlapping scheduling rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In addition to the maximum vacation pay that he would have received had he worked the full year' is a generous but definite formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-B.4's twenty-day cap 'in any one office' appears to be overridden here without saying so.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line incorporation of undocumented 'present practices' — vague by construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 13-B.2's requirement that 'the days of the vacation period shall be consecutive', which splitting necessarily contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three separate rules packed together; 'in any one office' is a meaningful limit and the holiday rule is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-B.2(b)'s death benefit and 20-D's holiday-in-vacation rule both interact with this cap, and 20-D cross-refers here for holiday pay.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise effective-year mapping.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Up to the termination date of this Agreement' aligns with Section 19's March 30, 1984 end date; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow crediting rule with two provisos; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13-B.2's treatment of compensation absences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any work lying outside the operations set forth in Section 2 hereof performed under the jurisdiction of a foreman' is a curious hybrid — non-unit work but under a unit foreman — and the qualifier's placement is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-A.1/2-B define the covered operations and 2-K bars non-unit employees from performing them, so this clause's scope depends on where the Section 2 line falls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise rate and rounding rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-H, 5-I, 5-K and 7-B set different multiples for Sunday and holiday work, so 'all overtime' at time and one-half is in tension with those doubled rates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is severely corrupted at the opening ('engaged in the net of any of the operations ... foF isher'), and the proportional-relation formula is convoluted even when reconstructed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-E.2 makes the same over-scale arrangements revocable at will by the Publisher, which largely negates the protection created here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision as reproduced is scrambled — its opening words are missing and the text of 13-F is spliced into the middle — so the operative sentence cannot be read straight through.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly undercuts 13-E.1's preservation of over-scale differentials by making any such arrangement modifiable or abrogable at the Publisher's will.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Two days' pay for such collection' is definite, though the parenthetical 'other than those now billing through the auditing department' incorporates an unstated present practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-A.1 excludes collectors where billing runs through the auditing department, matching this carve-out; 13-G handles shortages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Excessive or repeated shortages' and relief 'as it may deem proper' are vague, though the half-of-one-per-cent cap is hard-edged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Section 16 referral scheme and 13-F collections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The contribution base — a garbled percentage 'of each employee's rate per shift' — and the phrase 'each employee in the bargaining unit' are the operative measures, and both the rate and the unit boundary are contestable on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends entirely on Sections 2-A/2-B defining the bargaining unit and on 13-K.3 (which adds paid-leave days as contribution days) and 13-A.2's $6 fringe allocation; delinquency enforcement also routes through Section 16.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cost-shifting rule with a clear threshold, though it lacks a sentence-ending punctuation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13-H.1's employer contribution scheme; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining 'employee' to include any individual whose retirement was recognized by the Trustees is circular and potentially open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands the term beyond 13-H.1's 'each employee in the bargaining unit', creating two different meanings of 'employee' inside the same Fund section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other employers of individuals working under provisions substantially the same as those of this Agreement' is a genuinely vague eligibility test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrored by 13-I.2 for the Pension Fund; consistent, though it extends Fund participation beyond the signatories identified in the preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '8% of each employee's pay rate per shift for each shift worked by each employee in the bargaining unit' fixes the base by reference to an undefined unit boundary and to 'pay rate per shift' rather than actual pay.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The obligation's scope turns on Sections 2-A/2-B unit coverage, is enlarged by 13-K.3 (paid-leave days) and 13-A.4 (COLA included in fringes), and its enforcement route through the Joint Standing Committee sits against 16-A's thirty-day waiver rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantially the same as those as set forth herein' is vague and the sentence contains a doubled 'as those as'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 13-H.4 and subject to the Trust Agreement, which is an external document not reproduced here.
